spec.user_stories: - As the owner, I run `docker compose up` and get the API plus Postgres 17 without installing Python or Postgres. - As the owner, my entries and photos survive `docker compose down` and restarts (down without -v). - As the owner, the Docker setup does not collide with my local dev server (host 8000) or local Postgres (host 5432). - As a contributor, no real secrets are committed.
spec.acceptance_criteria: 1. Dockerfile builds from a python:3.12 slim base, installs requirements.txt (no new or changed Python dependencies), and copies backend/ and frontend/ so that backend/ and frontend/ are siblings under one root and uploads/ resolves to that same root (matching models.PROJECT_ROOT logic). Pass: inside the container, `/` serves index.html and `/static/...` works. 2. The container runs uvicorn main:app from the backend directory bound to 0.0.0.0 on a fixed container port (8000). No --reload. 3. compose.yaml defines exactly two services: `api` (built from the Dockerfile) and `db` (image postgres:17). 4. `db` has a pg_isready healthcheck; `api` uses depends_on with condition: service_healthy. Pass: on a cold `up`, api starts only after db is healthy and init_db succeeds with no connection-refused crash. 5. `api` receives DATABASE_URL pointing at the db service by compose service name (not localhost), using the same user, password and database as the db service. 6. Credentials: no literal real secret in committed files. Postgres user/password/db come from `${VAR:-default}` substitution with a clearly dev-only default (password default non-empty, e.g. a placeholder), overridable via shell env or a git-ignored .env. Justification: Postgres is not published to the host, so the default is reachable only inside the compose network. 7. Postgres is NOT published to the host (no `ports` on db). Pass: `docker compose config` shows no host port for db, and nothing binds host 5432. 8. api host port defaults to a value other than 8000 and 5432 (default 8080), overridable by an env var (e.g. `${API_PORT:-8080}`), mapped to container port 8000. Pass: http://localhost:8080/ returns the page while the local dev server on 8000 is unaffected. 9. Two top-level named volumes: one mounted at Postgres's data dir, one mounted at the app's uploads dir (the project-root uploads folder inside the container). No bind mounts to the host repo (the repo's uploads/ is never mounted). Pass: after creating an entry with a photo, `down` then `up` (same project name) still lists the entry and serves the photo. 10. The api process can write to the uploads volume (photo upload via POST /api/logs returns success in the container). 11. .dockerignore excludes at least .git, .venv, .claude, uploads, __pycache__/*.pyc, .env, .pytest_cache, and backend/tests is not required to be excluded but may be. Pass: build context does not contain these. 12. README: the Dockerfile and compose.yaml rows in the project structure no longer say "Not set up yet" (short accurate descriptions), and a short "Run with Docker" section (command, URL, port override, data persistence/`down -v` warning) is added. No other README changes. 13. No changes to backend/, frontend/, requirements.txt, .gitignore or CI workflow. (If .env must be ignored, it already is.)
spec.assumptions: - Default host port 8080 for api; Postgres unpublished (user can add a ports entry themselves if they want host access). Chosen over asking because it is easily changed and avoids both conflicts. - Default credentials via ${VAR:-default} chosen over a required env_file so `docker compose up` works with zero setup; .env remains optional. - Running as root vs non-root is the implementer's call provided criterion 10 holds. - Container-internal port is 8000 (isolated from the host's 8000). - requirements.txt includes pytest/httpx2; installing it as-is in the image is acceptable (no dependency changes allowed). - The db-name default is not `dailylog` collision-prone: compose uses its own volume, so the user's local dailylog database is never touched.
spec.edge_cases: - First start with empty volumes: init_db creates tables; uploads dir exists and is writable. - api restarted while db is down: fails and is retried or reported clearly (restart policy optional). - Password containing URL-special characters in DATABASE_URL (document default is URL-safe; note in README only if small). - Changing POSTGRES_PASSWORD after the volume is initialized does not change the existing DB password (Postgres behaviour); README one-liner optional. - Host port 8080 already in use: overridable via API_PORT. - Verification must use a distinct project name (e.g. -p t019verify) so volumes are isolated from anything else.

risks.risk: Named uploads volume permissions if the image runs as non-root: volume may be root-owned and uploads fail.
Placeholder default password committed; acceptable only because db is unpublished. If user later publishes 5432, they should override it.
Unpinned/slim base tag drift; pin to 3.12-slim and postgres:17 to match CI.
Docker-daemon availability on the verifier's machine.

spec.dependencies: Docker Engine with Compose v2; base images python:3.12-slim and postgres:17; existing requirements.txt, backend/, frontend/; DATABASE_URL contract in backend/main.py.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria (setup: 1-5; persistence: 9-10; no conflicts: 7-8; no secrets: 6). All criteria are observable through compose config, curl, or a down/up cycle. Biggest risk: uploads volume permissions and the placeholder-password choice; port 8080 is an assumption the user may want different, though it is overridable.
